answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with an entangled task graph: every job's input is another agent's output, so work flows like meltwater from a glacier across a wide horizon toward one oasis of finished goods. A farm that invents thousands of identities still forms a closed loop, because its members only consume each other's fake outputs and never touch upstream work. Honest agents plug into the open graph once and inherit trusted inputs cheaply, while a Sybil operator must fabricate the whole supply chain for every fake, paying the full cost of a real economy per identity.
